intro: Rule-based sentence segmentation can be useful when its limitations are explicit. A short scanner gives reproducible boundaries without requiring a language model.
task: Split on .!? runs and retain closing punctuation without claiming linguistic completeness.
requirements: Scan text left to right. A maximal run of .!? ends a sentence; include any immediately following closing quotes or brackets from the set double-quote, single-quote, ), ], }. Trim outer Unicode whitespace from each sentence and omit empty pieces. Return a final unterminated fragment if present. Do not infer abbreviations or require a space after punctuation.
Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Consume an entire punctuation run and then its immediate closing characters before cutting.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Keep a final fragment even if it has no terminator.

explanation: Rule-based sentence segmentation can be useful when its limitations are explicit. A short scanner gives reproducible boundaries without requiring a language model.
Periods in abbreviations or decimal numbers still split here. This deliberately narrow contract teaches stateful scanning rather than promising linguistic sentence detection.
